1.why: All six screens are static cards with no animations, carousels, or pop-up overlays.

2.why: Each screen has a large dark-blue heading, a highlighted info box and a single filled primary button, so key elements stand out, though the black activity log competes visually.

3.why: Each step shows only one task and one clear primary action, making the next thing to do easy to locate, but the token/log text adds noise.

4.why: Rules like the 12-character password policy are shown on screen, yet she must carry a long recovery token and a 6-digit code from the log into fields across a 6-step sequence with no progress indicator.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any screen.

6.why: Apart from the recovery code being pre-filled in step 2, nothing familiar or saved (e.g., masked email, account name) is displayed for recognition.

7.why: Sentences are short, in plain language and rendered in a large readable font with good contrast.

8.why: No error or validation message is visible in any of the six screenshots, so the claim cannot be observed to hold.

9.why: There is guidance text and a stated password rule, but no concrete example of what to type (no sample address, sample password, or code format illustration).

10.why: The two available paths — 'Send recovery instructions' and 'I have a recovery code' — are plainly labelled, though no biometric/face option exists.

11.why: Every screen presents at most two buttons and one or two fields, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Steps 5 and 6 explicitly confirm the outcome ('Your account access has been confirmed', 'Privacy conditions accepted'), although saving the new password leads straight to MFA with no stated confirmation.

13.why: Short helper/info boxes explain each new step (safety notice, password rules, code delivery explanation).

14.why: Only step 2 offers a 'Back' button; other screens show no back, cancel, resend-code, or retry affordance.

15.why: Header, card layout, typography, colour scheme, and button styling are identical across all six steps.
